title: POC scoping - success criteria signoff
summary: Redwood and Helios finalize POC acceptance tests and go/no-go thresholds. Discussed workload sizing, benchmark harness, reporting format, timeline and roles. Agreed on weekly benchmark reports, pass thresholds for latency, throughput, cost and accuracy; security docs and contract items to be exchanged. Next steps: Redwood to run baseline benchmarks, share benchmark sheet and reporting template; Helios to provide sample traffic and secure test dataset; schedule setup kickoff and 2-week pilot start window.
topics: Success criteria sign-off (latency, throughput, cost, quality)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-04-22 15:00 PDT / Duration: ~57m / Recording: yes
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Marco Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Helios Head of AI), Tom Nguyen (Helios SRE), Janelle Ortiz (Helios PM)

[00:00] Alicia: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, we wanted to use this time to lock the success criteria and confirm acceptance tests for the POC, last-minute things?
[00:12] Priya: yeah thanks, we've gone through the doc, I think main ask is we need clear go/no-go thresholds and the reporting we can give to the execs, like weekly scoreboard.
[00:20] Marco: totally, we'll propose a reporting template — CSV + latency histograms + accuracy dashboard — but first let's align on the thresholds.
[00:30] Janelle: for timelines, real simple: we want pilot start in two weeks and 2-week run, is that still realistic?
[00:38] Alicia: yes we can hit that if Helios can provide sample traffic and the 3k annotated test prompts by Monday.
[00:47] Tom: small caveat — our security team needs the VPC deployment details, but for the benchmark we'll start in our staging VPC and only push to Private deployment later.
[00:56] Marco: sounds good; we'll use Redwood Dedicated in the staging VPC config for parity with production.
[01:05] Priya: ok, let's get into thresholds. We proposed a pass if 3 of 4 buckets meet target: latency (p95), throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and quality measured by evaluation set. 3/4 required to go. Clarify?
[01:18] Marco: yes that's what we recommend; the exact numbers we suggested in the doc were: p95 latency < 250ms for 512-token context, throughput >= 100 req/min sustained, cost <= $0.15 per 1k tokens served (including batching), and accuracy: >= 95% pass rate on the curated eval set (fuzzy match for structured outputs).
[01:36] Priya: that cost threshold seems aggressive — is that host-only or includes storage / KV cache overhead?
[01:42] Marco: that number is model-serving cost only — excludes S3 storage and egress. It includes batching and KV cache effects we measured in prior runs.
[01:50] Priya: ok, we'll flag as 'model-serving unit cost' in the report.
[01:55] Janelle: how will we measure accuracy? The eval set isn't just single-token match, some structured fields are fuzzy — we need an automated scorer and a manual review sample.
[02:06] Marco: agreed — we'll use the eval harness: automated metrics (exact + fuzzy match thresholds) and then sample 200 outputs for human review; acceptance needs >=95% automated pass and human sample mean >=92% agreement.
[02:20] Priya: that seems reasonable. Put that in the acceptance tests.
[02:24] Alicia: noted. Next, workload sizing — Tom, you mentioned peak patterns?
[02:29] Tom: yeah our daytime peak is approx 180 req/min but average is 40 req/min, with spiky bursts to 250 for ~2 min. The POC we'll scale down to a 100 req/min steady-state profile with occasional 200+ bursts to test autoscaling.
[02:41] Marco: perfect, we'll run benchmarks with the provided traffic profile, and also synthetic tail-latency workloads to exercise KV cache and batching.
[02:50] Priya: and the benchmark harness — are you going to publish the raw results? We need raw CSV + histograms + the run config.
[02:58] Marco: yes we'll share a benchmark sheet link (we'll send access to the Google sheet) with per-run stats: p50/p90/p95/p99, tokens served, avg cost per 1k tokens, fail rates, and the raw traces (sampled).
[03:10] Janelle: format for exec review: one-pager summary + attached CSVs and a short slide on recommendations?
[03:16] Alicia: we'll produce that template: weekly one-pager, CSV export, and a short slack-friendly summary.
[03:22] Priya: good. On acceptance tests: how do we treat regressions? If accuracy drops 3 points but latency improves, does that fail?
[03:30] Marco: acceptance logic is rule-based: to pass overall you need 3/4 buckets. So if accuracy fails but latency, throughput, and cost pass, overall POC passes; however, any security or data-loss issue is automatic fail. Also we'll flag any regression >5% on accuracy as high risk and require mitigation.
[03:46] Priya: understood. For security checks, we need SOC2 type II docs, SSO integration notes, KMS/HSM approaches for keys, and audit logs.
[03:55] Alicia: we'll send the security pack and a short integration runbook for our VPC/private deployment. Expect that by EOD tomorrow.
[04:02] Tom: we'll need an IP allowlist and dedicated subnets for the pilot. Can you provide the CIDR ranges you'll use?
[04:08] Marco: yes, we'll share the staging CIDR and the connector steps; it's in the runbook.
[04:13] Janelle: timeline recap?
[04:16] Alicia: action timeline: Helios provides sample traffic + eval set by Monday (2025-04-28), Redwood runs baseline and shares benchmark harness + initial runs by Thursday (2025-05-01), kickoff infra setup this week, pilot start target 2025-05-05, 2-week run finishes 2025-05-19, go/no-go decision meeting 2025-05-21.
[04:35] Priya: can we compress to start 2025-05-02? Exec wants faster but ok we'll try.
[04:39] Alicia: we'll push to accelerate if Helios can get inputs earlier.
[04:43] Marco: one technical note — model variant fallbacks: we'll configure automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant if tail latency spikes above 700ms for >30s; that will be part of the resilience plan but falls outside acceptance metrics unless it masks capacity issues.
[04:57] Tom: ok, document that as a mitigation not a pass criteria.
[05:02] Priya: what about reporting cadence? Weekly report + final acceptance package?
[05:07] Alicia: weekly reports every Friday, final acceptance package after the 2-week run including raw CSVs, histograms, config, and the one-pager with decision recommendation.
[05:15] Janelle: who signs off? Priya or procurement?
[05:18] Priya: I'll do the technical sign-off and procurement will do commercial. We'll loop procurement in before 05-21.
[05:23] Marco: noted. Also small transcription note: some of the model names in the doc may be spelled incorrectly in the auto-export; we'll attach the canonical model IDs in the benchmark sheet.
[05:33] Alicia: ok let's capture action items and owners now.
[05:35] Priya: quick question: success criteria - do we show per-route thresholds or aggregate?
[05:40] Marco: both — aggregate for execs, per-route for dev teams. We'll include per-route p95 and fail rates in the CSV.
[05:47] Janelle: sounds good.
[05:49] Alicia: recap: benchmarks to include p50/p90/p95/p99, throughput, cost per 1k, accuracy metrics (auto + sampled manual review), and a pass/fail summary per-bucket and overall. We'll send the template moments after the call.
[06:02] Priya: ok, I'm comfortable signing the acceptance criteria as discussed (3/4 rule, thresholds as listed). Put that in the doc and we'll sign off.
[06:10] Alicia: great, we'll update the POC doc and send for e-sign. Anything else?
[06:15] Tom: no, just the VPC CIDR and the runbook.
[06:18] Marco: we'll share the benchmark sheet link and the runbook.
[06:21] Alicia: thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with links and the action items. Meeting end.

Note: transcript contains natural speech artifacts; occasional mis-hearings in auto-transcript (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "kay vee cache" in some lines).
